description: A precursor protein is cleaved to produce a chain protein. Precursors include polyproteins, proenzymes, and prohormones.

common_properties.name: sources
common_properties.description: Sources contributing the relationship; UniProt is the source of these precursor–chain relationships.

common_properties.name: last_updated
common_properties.description: Time the relationship was created or its source attribution last changed.

source_contributions.scope: Cleavage products represented by UniProt chain annotations, including polyproteins, prohormones, and two-chain proenzymes, without filtering by organism or review status. Full-span chain annotations are included. Relationships can involve obsolete proteins; coverage of pairs with both proteins obsolete is history-dependent.
source_contributions.description: Each relationship connects the top-level UniProt precursor entry to a chain product. Intermediate precursor-to-product relationships are not inferred, even when a product biologically derives from an intermediate precursor. Chain positions are available on the chain Protein node rather than the relationship.
